clue.text: "I will avoid UN aid questions," initially annoyed every critic of Trump!

definitions.note: Trump repeatedly dismissed his critics with this insult, so it fits any one of them

indicators.note: annoyed here means stirred up, so the letters of the quoted words are jumbled
initially asks for only the opening letter of questions

explanation.surface: A quoted refusal to answer about UN aid, said to irritate Trump's critics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'annoyed' shuffles IWILLAVOIDUNAID plus Q, the first letter that 'initially' takes from 'questions'.
explanation.definitionFit: Donald Trump's habitual put-down for opponents was this phrase, so it describes how he labelled each critic.

clue.text: Real excited welcoming old and great leader

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the shuffled letters go around the other pieces
excited means agitated, so the letters of real are stirred about

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
ex- is a prefix meaning former or old

explanation.surface: Someone genuinely thrilled to greet an aged and distinguished commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' turns REAL into ALER, and 'welcoming' has it take in EX and AND.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander the Great, the Macedonian conqueror, is the classic great leader.

clue.text: Best work — it's about gender mostly

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word it is read backwards

parts.note: gives it, the 's standing for is and joining the pieces

indicators.note: mostly means losing the last letter of the word for this gender

parts.note: male is one gender

explanation.surface: A comment on someone's finest work being mostly concerned with gender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses IT to TI; 'mostly' trims MALE to MAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something optimal is the most favourable possible, i.e. the best.

clue.text: Wheeled king in around eleven o'clock at first

definitions.note: describes a king who was put on a wheel

indicators.note: around means the word in is placed outside the other letters

parts.note: XI is eleven in Roman numerals

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of o'clock

explanation.surface: A king being pushed in on wheels at about eleven o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Zeus bound King Ixion to a fiery wheel for ever, which is why 'Wheeled' fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeus punished this Thessalian king by binding him to an eternally turning wheel.

clue.text: Axe a throwback, sort of?

parts.note: read as throw back: a throw is a lob, and back turns it round
the suffix -ish means sort of, as in greenish

explanation.surface: Asking whether an axe is a kind of throwback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throwback' looks like one word meaning a reversion, but split it: a throw (LOB) sent back gives BOL.
explanation.definitionFit: To axe a policy or scheme is to scrap it completely.

clue.text: Always opens containers holding energy drinks

indicators.note: holding means the combined letters contain the symbol for energy
opens means the word for always goes inside, splitting the containers apart

parts.note: bags are containers
ever means always, as in ever hopeful
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Someone who always opens cans or boxes of energy drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opens' puts EVER in BAGS for BEVERAGS; 'holding' takes in E.
explanation.definitionFit: Beverages are any liquids for drinking, a formal synonym for drinks.

clue.text: Brash girl's behind advert regularly featured

indicators.note: featured means included, so the picked letters sit inside the word for behind

parts.note: behind means late, as in behind schedule

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of advert

explanation.surface: A loud young woman appeared at the back of an advert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of advert; 'featured' sets them inside the word for behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladette is a young woman who behaves in a loud, boisterous, laddish way.

clue.text: Say no more, a stunning hat

parts.note: sh is the call for silence, telling someone to say no more
KO is a knockout, the stunning blow in boxing

explanation.surface: Someone cuts off chatter to admire a stunning hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A shako is a tall cylindrical military cap with a peak and plume.

clue.text: Love big boobs, lad? That's more likely than not

parts.note: love is nil, the letter O, in tennis
DD is a large bra cup size
a son is a lad, a boy

explanation.surface: A cheeky line suggesting a lad is probably fond of a large chest.
explanation.definitionFit: In betting, a favourite at odds-on is rated more likely to win than lose.

clue.text: See 25
See 1
Working so, I'm extremely respected — a titan in government

indicators.note: working means being worked over, so these letters are reshaped
extremely takes the two end letters of respected

explanation.surface: A respected titan boasting of being hard at work in government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' looks like a description of the titan, but it is the anagram signal; 'extremely' supplies just the two ends of respected.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage the administration is the executive branch, the government of the day.

clue.text: Confused and burdened when leader's away

indicators.note: says the first letter of the word for burdened is removed

parts.note: saddled means burdened, as with debt

explanation.surface: Someone muddled and weighed down when the boss is absent.
explanation.definitionFit: An addled mind is muddled, unable to think clearly.

clue.text: Hairy dog exercising with a nurse

definitions.note: used in the informal sense of risky or scary

indicators.note: exercising means putting through movements, so the letters are moved about

explanation.surface: A shaggy dog being walked by a nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hairy' looks like it describes the dog's coat, but it is slang for perilous.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairy situation, in informal speech, is frightening and full of risk.

clue.text: Ignores info about cancelled services round college

indicators.note: about means the word for info is turned around

parts.note: gen is slang for information

indicators.note: round means the services go around the letter for college

parts.note: in tennis a let is a serve that is voided and replayed

explanation.surface: Someone disregards news about withdrawn services near a college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cancelled services' suggests axed trains, but it is tennis: a let is a serve that is voided and replayed.
explanation.definitionFit: To neglect something is to fail to pay it attention, to disregard it.

clue.text: National leader of absolute principle — is every single person in support?

indicators.note: in a down clue the later pieces sit below and so prop up the first

parts.note: the Tao is the absolute principle underlying the universe in Taoism
each means every single one

explanation.surface: Asking whether a leader of firm principle has everyone behind them.
explanation.walkthrough: The Taoiseach is the prime minister of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Taoiseach is the head of the Irish government, Ireland's national leader.

clue.text: Image control is working with Her Majesty … and one of her guests?

parts.note: PR, public relations, is the management of image
on means working, as a machine that is on
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A spin doctor at work for the Queen, and someone she entertains.
explanation.walkthrough: British convicts are said to be held 'at Her Majesty's pleasure', so the inmate is wryly her guest.
explanation.definitionFit: British jails are HM Prisons, so an inmate is ironically a guest of the Queen.

clue.text: In decline, one pre-eminent in evil?

parts.note: sin is evil, wrongdoing
a king is one pre-eminent, the top figure in a field

explanation.surface: Asking whether a fading figure was once the master of wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second half as a king of sin, top dog in wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinking business or reputation is going downhill, failing steadily.

clue.text: Supporting group's about to get better

indicators.note: about means going around, so the band's name surrounds the word for supporting

parts.note: REM is the American rock group; the 's stands for is
for means supporting, as in voting for

explanation.surface: A backing band is about to improve.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking 'about' as the prefix for concerning is the natural first move, but nothing then gives the rest; the band R.E.M. goes round 'for'.
explanation.definitionFit: To reform is to mend one's ways, to improve one's conduct.

clue.text: Train toilet hacks regularly used on return journey

indicators.note: a return journey goes back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: loo is British slang for toilet

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of hacks

explanation.surface: Train toilets regularly used by hacks travelling home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes HCS from HaCkS; 'on return journey' reverses LOOHCS.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to train or coach them.

clue.text: 1A/10? Yes and no

parts.note: the cross-reference is the dim person of 1 and 10; and no is half of nous, a word for wit

explanation.walkthrough: 1A/10 is the Trump insult in the first clue. NO is half of NOUS (wit), so 'Yes and no' is half a wit.
explanation.definitionFit: A halfwit is a foolish, dim person, just what a low-intelligence insult describes.

clue.text: "Shabby, if clean" — how Pres referred to public figure for a spell

definitions.text: referred to public figure for a spell
definitions.note: describes a famous person as named, and misspelt, by Trump

indicators.note: shabby means ragged, so these letters are knocked about

explanation.surface: Trump's tweeted misspelling of the heir to the throne, roughed up.
explanation.walkthrough: In 2019 Trump tweeted about meeting the 'Prince of Whales'; 'for a spell' hints at the bad spelling. The heir's title is Prince of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Trump's tweet named Prince Charles with an extra H, giving this misspelt royal title.

clue.text: Up in jungle targeting animal

indicators.note: in a down clue up means reading from the bottom, so the letters are reversed
in shows the letters sit within jungle targeting

explanation.surface: A beast high in the jungle stalking its prey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' picks LETAR from jungLE TARgeting; 'Up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The ratel is the honey badger, a fierce African and Asian mammal.

clue.text: American animated by base, right?

parts.note: home is a base, as in baseball's home plate

explanation.surface: An American roused by a military base, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: Homer Simpson is the cartoon dad of The Simpsons.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer Simpson is a cartoon American, an animated character.

clue.text: Woman returns after clear message (delivered starkly?)

indicators.note: after puts the reversed name behind the word for clear

parts.note: to strip a room is to clear it

indicators.note: returns means the name is read backwards

parts.note: Margo is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman comes back after a clear message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns MARGO into OGRAM. Stark naked is the pun in 'starkly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip-o-gram is a greeting delivered by someone who undresses, so stark naked.

clue.text: I didn't hear 10's in clear — I'm surprised

parts.note: what? is a blunt way to say I didn't catch that

indicators.note: in puts the numeral inside the word for clear

parts.note: net means clear, as in net profit after deductions
X is ten in Roman numerals; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Someone who missed a remark about number 10 and is taken aback.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' looks like a cross-reference to 10 across, but here it is just the numeral X.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation expresses astonishment at yet another development, like saying I'm surprised.

clue.text: Poet from Spain on first

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain
in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
1st is the abbreviation for first

explanation.surface: A poet who comes from Spain, appearing first.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side (on side) is the half of the field behind the batter's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegist writes elegies, mournful poems.

clue.text: Wife needs gag — poor fellow!

parts.note: to gag is to retch

explanation.surface: A wife needs a joke, sympathy for her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gag' looks like a joke or a muzzle, but here it means to heave.
explanation.definitionFit: A wretch is an unfortunate, pitiable person.
